overview.headline: Using CPI ratios to measure purchasing power and constant dollars

keyPoints.point: Students learn that the purchasing power of a dollar in 2022 was about 92.6 percent of its purchasing power in 2021.
keyPoints.quote: The purchasing power of a dollar in 2022 was about 92.6 percent of the purchasing power of a dollar in 2021.

keyPoints.point: Students learn that purchasing power declined about 7.4 percent between 2021 and 2022 because of inflation.
keyPoints.quote: This means that the purchasing power of the dollar declined about 7.4 percent between 2021 and 2022 because of inflation.

keyPoints.point: Students learn that converting nominal amounts into constant dollars uses multiplying each dollar amount by a ratio of price indexes with one year as the base.
keyPoints.quote: This is done by multiplying each dollar amount by a ratio of price indexes, using one year as the base, as shown below.

keyPoints.point: Students learn that nominal median household income rose from 49,276 to 70,784 between 2010 and 2021, an increase of 43.6 percent, while real growth was more modest.
keyPoints.quote: while the nominal U.S. median household income rose from $49,276 to $70,784 from 2010 to 2021, an increase of 43.6 percent

keyTerms.gloss: share of goods a dollar can buy, shown by purchasing power change over time
keyTerms.quote: The purchasing power of a dollar in 2022 was about 92.6 percent of the purchasing power of a dollar in 2021.

keyTerms.gloss: index that measures average price change used in the CPI-U ratio
keyTerms.quote: multiply the dollar amount by the ratio of the CPI-U U.S. city average all items index values for December 2022 and December 2021

keyTerms.gloss: dollars expressed in prices of a chosen base year, shown as Constant dollars values
current dollar amounts before adjusting for price changes, called nominal dollars
keyTerms.quote: it is frequently necessary to convert current or nominal dollars into constant or real dollars.

keyTerms.gloss: general rise in prices that causes purchasing power to decline because of inflation
